A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same trajectory-distillation work, renamed from TraFlow to SCoT, with substantial revisions. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TraFlow generation results on CIFAR-10, FFHQ-64, and ImageNet, together with ablations, training curves, and generated samples (Tables 4-7 and Figures 2-4).

after.justification: v2 reports original SCoT benchmark results and training analyses in Tables 2-6, plus throughput measurements and ImageNet generation samples in Appendix D.

M1.justification: v1's separate output, velocity, and consistency objective becomes a velocity-plus-integrated-soft-consistency objective, with output matching folded into consistency (v1 Equation 12; v2 Equations 3-4). Soft matching was already an option in v1, but v2 specifies EMA-decoded endpoint matching and introduces adaptive weighting and a clipped velocity-weight variant. The basic projection and sampling procedure remain.

E1.justification: Reported evaluation coverage contracts from CIFAR-10, FFHQ-64, and ImageNet to CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. The FFHQ-64 generation comparison and throughput results disappear, although its metadata remains in v2 Table 10. CelebA mentions in v1 do not establish a separate reported experiment.

E2.justification: v2 adds one- and two-step CTM comparisons, explicitly marked as using GAN loss, on both retained benchmarks. ImageNet additionally gains conditional and unconditional Shortcut comparisons, while the two-step CT comparator from v1 Table 6 disappears. These are substantive comparator changes within retained experiments.

E3.justification: Small-student experiments are replaced by substantially larger configurations. Reported CIFAR-10 settings change from batch size 64, AdamW, and RK45 to batch size 512, Adam, and Heun, with a stated 130k-iteration budget (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 8). New ImageNet analyses specify 6k evaluation samples and introduce sFID reporting; CIFAR-10 comparisons replace IS with an NLL column. These are reported protocol changes, not evidence that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1's CIFAR-10 initialization, teacher, divergence, loss-component, and Euler-solver ablations and convergence plots are removed. v2 adds ImageNet training-stage analyses for consistency and combined losses, a three-way velocity-weighting comparison, and qualitative training-progress comparisons (Tables 4-6; Appendix D). The questions and supporting evidence change substantially.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, standard deviations, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experimental results. Both primarily present point estimates.

E6.justification: CIFAR-10 one-step FIDs of 5.8 and 4.5 in v1 are replaced by 2.40 in v2; ImageNet one- and two-step FIDs of 12 are replaced by 4.80 and 2.60 under changed model configurations. These are not controlled same-setting gains. The ImageNet two-step CD entry also changes from 4.70 to 6.20. Numerous training, weighting, and throughput results are added or replaced, while FFHQ-64 results are removed.

T1.justification: The formal loss definitions are revised: velocity matching extends from a local derivative at t to a derivative evaluated at sampled terminal s, and consistency gains explicit EMA-decoded targets and time domains (v1 Equations 9-11; v2 Equations 2-3). No theorem or proof is added. Appendix A's theoretical motivation largely restates the parameterization and explains the losses intuitively.

C1.justification: The central claim remains that combining trajectory straightness and consistency enables fast, high-quality generation. v2 recasts the three-target contribution as a two-objective construction and adds an explicit claim to be the first to produce straight and consistent trajectories. Claims about compact models and few-step generation remain broadly intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving trajectory curvature, soft versus local consistency, second-order gradient instability, loss clipping, and GAN-related comparison qualifications. It also explicitly states that training from scratch was not explored because of resource constraints. Some new interpretations conflict with the evidence: Section 4.6 claims adaptive-weighting FID increases late in training, whereas Table 6 shows continued decreases.

D1.justification: v2 adds teacher-checkpoint access information, explicit autograd usage, attention-loading and xformers implementation details, ImageNet training settings, and disclosure of DSM training. Conversely, several per-size U-Net and regularization settings from v1 disappear. Reproducibility information changes substantially, although v2's student EMA rate is inconsistent between Section 4.1 (0.9999) and Table 8 (0.999).

R1.justification: The principal CTM, reflow, and Shortcut positioning and three-category related-work taxonomy are retained. v2 refines the discussion of shared objectives, adds references including the Fan et al. survey, Sajjadi et al., and several Wu works, and removes references including Tract and AMED-Solver. Moving related work to Appendix B is primarily structural.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around SCoT terminology. Related work and notation move to the appendices, and the original technical supplement is reorganized into Appendices A-E with a contents page. This is substantial rewriting and restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. New comparative trajectory schematics replace the earlier loss illustration; CIFAR-10 training plots and sample grids give way to ImageNet training-stage grids. Benchmark tables change metric columns and grouping, new analysis tables are introduced, and notation and throughput displays move to the appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 offers clearer exposition, more implementation information, closer CTM/Shortcut comparisons, and useful new weighting analyses. However, it removes FFHQ-64 and small-model evidence while retaining compact-model claims, and introduces material reporting inconsistencies. For example, Section 4.6 describes worsening adaptive-weighting FID despite Table 6 showing 15.3 to 6.2, and the stated EMA rates conflict. These gains and losses affect both scientific support and reproducibility, so the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
